title: Should we be syncing our workouts to our menstrual cycles?
description:
We’ve seen more and more women talking about cycle-syncing. It’s where you adjust your diet and work outs to match the different phases of your period. Things like eating more in certain phases or taking it easy in others.

But does cycle-syncing help you get better results? Does the science back it up or is it just another wellness trend and rule book for women to follow?

BBC reporter Zara Salaria takes us through what cycle syncing is, we hear from people who have tried it and a doctor breaks it down for us: does it work?

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討經期同步 cycle syncing 運動趨勢與其背後的科學依據。 BBC 記者 Zara Salaria 與主持人 Hannah Gelbart 討論了在月經期、濾泡期、排卵期及黃體期等不同階段調整飲食與訓練的流行做法。雖然生理週期的荷爾蒙變化確實會影響女性的體能、情緒與症狀，但女性健康專家 Faye Bate 醫師指出，目前缺乏科學證據支持統一的經期同步訓練公式。專家與受訪者強調，每位女性的生理週期與身體反應皆獨一無二，建議大家著重於傾聽自身感受並記錄個人變化，而非盲目遵守網路上的嚴格計畫。
summaryEn: This episode explores the trend of cycle syncing—adjusting workouts and diet to match the different phases of the menstrual cycle (menstrual, follicular, ovulation, and luteal). BBC reporter Zara Salaria, host Hannah Gelbart, and medical doctor Faye Bate discuss whether this popular wellness practice is backed by science. While hormonal shifts cause real changes in energy, mood, and physical symptoms, there is no scientific evidence supporting a rigid, one-size-fits-all cycle syncing formula. Because menstrual cycles vary greatly between individuals and from month to month, experts advise women to listen to their own bodies and track individual patterns rather than following strict online rules.
